title: VSCode silently switches to Microsoft models, ignoring BYO agent configuration
content:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes
What is the issue
I bring my own models when developing using VSCode. This includes locally hosted models and cost effective API models depending on the context.
VSCode overrides my agent selection every time I start a new chat. This makes me unintentionally use mai-code-flash free tier, which collects data (unacceptable in commercial and private contexts).
System
Version: 1.142.0-insider (user setup)
Commit: d2a9268
Date: 2026-10-08T09:31:50-07:00

Steps to Reproduce:
- Set your agent to Local and pick your model
- Click on new chat
- VSCode automatically changes agent configuration back to Copilot

report.summary: A VS Code Insider user reports that new chats silently reset their chosen local or BYO model back to Copilot's MAI-code-flash, raising privacy and vendor-lock-in concerns.
report.background: As AI coding assistants mature, developers increasingly configure bring-your-own-key (BYOK) or local models for cost, latency, and compliance. VS Code's Copilot Chat supports model pickers and agent modes, but default behavior can steer users toward Microsoft-hosted models. Free tiers are often subsidized by data collection, which is unacceptable in commercial or private contexts. GitHub issue #340651 describes an Insider build where agent selection resets to Copilot on new chat, overriding local or API-based configuration. The reporter says this causes unintentional use of mai-code-flash free tier, which they believe collects data. The issue occurs with extensions disabled and includes precise reproduction steps. It highlights tension between vendor defaults, monetization, and user control. If reproducible broadly, it becomes a governance and trust problem, not just a UI bug.
key_points: The report says VS Code resets a user's chosen agent or model to Copilot every time a new chat starts. Reproduction is simple: select Local, pick a model, open a new chat, and the configuration reverts. The behavior occurs even with all extensions disabled, suggesting a built-in Copilot or core setting rather than third-party interference.

The user's main concern is privacy and compliance. Falling back to mai-code-flash free tier may send prompts and code to Microsoft-hosted services, which the reporter says collects data. For commercial, regulated, or private work, unintended routing to a cloud model can violate policies, NDAs, or data-residency requirements.

The issue reflects a broader BYO-model conflict. Developers adopt local models, API keys, and routers such as OpenRouter to control cost and data flow. When an IDE silently overrides those choices, it undermines trust and makes bring-your-own configuration feel unreliable and unsafe for sensitive work.

The report is from VS Code 1.142.0-insider, so behavior may change before stable release. However, Insider builds often surface defaults that later ship broadly. Microsoft has not publicly confirmed the issue, so scope, intent, and whether it is a bug or policy default remain unverified at this time.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is another flashpoint over default model routing. As assistants become gateways to models, vendors can nudge users toward first-party services, affecting competition and monetization. For developers, the practical impact is lost time, unexpected costs, and compliance risk; teams should audit settings, use managed profiles, and consider alternatives that respect BYOK. For regular users, the risk is subtler: prompts may leave their machine without clear consent. If VS Code confirms the behavior, expect pressure for transparent model selection, persistent BYOK, and stronger data-governance controls. If not, it is still a warning to verify which model is actually serving each chat.
report.tools: Watch GitHub issue #340651 for updates. For BYOK and local workflows, evaluate Continue.dev, Cline, Roo Code, and Aider, which offer explicit model configuration. Ollama and LM Studio run local models; LiteLLM or OpenRouter can proxy API models with logging controls. Review VS Code settings for Copilot Chat model persistence and enterprise policies. These alternatives do not guarantee no telemetry, so audit each tool's data handling before use.
